title: One Tap to Sign In, Zero adb to Update | vitalii.no
description:
How Android's Credential Manager replaced a PIN login, and a self-update check replaced plugging phones into a laptop.

Every new build of the native app meant connecting phones to a laptop and running a manual install, three phones at a time. On top of that, the only way to log in was a PIN, with no shortcut for the Google account already signed into the phone.

I added Credential Manager, which hands a Google ID token straight to the page so sign-in happens with one tap, keeping the PIN login only as a fallback. A new update-checker class polls a published manifest file and installs a newer build automatically when one is available. A GitHub Actions workflow now builds the app on every push and publishes it to a URL served straight from the project's own domain, so installing it the first time only needs a browser.

What used to take three manual installs per release, cable and laptop included, is now zero.
